subject: Change stacked bar ordering with a variable

messages.author: 9c9b5f9c6aaa025d
messages.subject: Change stacked bar ordering with a variable
parts:
Hi,
I am trying to build a stacked bar plot using a variable for the fill field. I would like to reverse the order of the stacking (not the order of the legend). According to the documentation (http://docs.ggplot2.org/0.9.3/aes_group_order.html) and Winston's Cookbook 3.7, you can do this by using aes(order = desc(Field)). However, how do you do this if the Field is a variable, i.e., I have been using aes_string for everything up to this point? Note, at the point I am trying to do this, I don't have access to the raw data, so reversing the order of a factor before calling ggplot is not a great solution for me. 

For example,
df <- data.frame(x = sample(c("foo", "bar"), 20, TRUE), y = sample(1:20), z = sample(c("a","b"), 20,TRUE));
fill_field <- "z";
p <- ggplot(df, aes(x)) + geom_histogram(aes_string(fill = fill_field));
# In the stacking, I want the green on the bottom and the red on top (to match the legend)
# Works, but I don't really know the field name explicitly, it is in a a string
p + aes(order = desc(z))
# Does not change anything 
p + aes(order = desc(fill_field))
p + aes_string(order = desc(fill_field))

Thanks,
Doug

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re: Change stacked bar ordering with a variable
parts:
On Mon, Apr 29, 2013 at 8:56 AM, Doug Mitarotonda <dougmit...@gmail.com> wrote:
p + aes_string(order = desc(fill_field))

aes_string requires a string as input so I think you just need to build it around your variable. 

p + aes_string(order = paste("desc(", fill_field, ")", sep=""))
